question: In spite of years of reports by fishers and the Maltese authorities with respect to illegal fishing and aggression by Tunisian-flagged vessels in the Mediterranean, engaged in common dolphinfish (coryphaena hippurus) fisheries, little action has been taken by the General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean (GFCM) Compliance Committee to rectify this long-standing situation.

On 19 August 2025, Maltese media reported that the European Fisheries Control Agency (EFCA) patrol vessel ‘Ocean Sentinel’ had successfully traced and identified Tunisian vessels engaged in illegal fishing of common dolphinfish using fishing aggregating devices. This constitutes clear evidence, gathered by the EFCA itself, of potential non-compliance by Tunisian vessels with GFCM rules. 1.
What was the potential non-compliance by these Tunisian vessels as detected by the EFCA?

Will the Commission raise these cases during the upcoming GFCM Compliance Committee meeting in November 2025, and demand enforcement by the Tunisian authorities against these vessels, thereby ensuring that Maltese and Italian fishers start to receive justice for years of inaction?

What steps does the Commission intend to take as a follow-up to this case, as well as to other similar cases that occurred this year but were not detected by the EFCA, to prevent future incidents, particularly those involving fishing during the closed season?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.12.2025) The Commission consistently promotes the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing at regional level, as well as the improvement of compliance with the regional fisheries management rules to promote effectively the level playing field amongst all operators.

In 2024, Recommendation 46/2023/171 of the General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean (GFCM), establishing an international joint inspection and surveillance (JIS) scheme for common dolphinfish fisheries, entered into force. The European Fisheries Control Agency (EFCA) is coordinating the participation of the EU in the scheme as regards the deployment of means.

As presented during the annual session of the GFCM Compliance Committee (CoC) (3-4 November 2025)2, the implementation of the JIS scheme in 2025 delivered 39 inspection reports. Among these, eight inspections involved Tunisian-flagged vessels, six of which revealed infringements such as missing catch records, fishing without a license, or misreporting.

Five of these cases led to follow-up measures including sanctions against captains, seizure of non-compliant equipment and fishery products, and vessel detention. The Commission sent a follow-up letter to Tunisia, as flag State, regarding the enforcement actions.
At the GFCM annual session (4-9 November 2025), upon a proposal made by the EU, the GFCM listed the vessel ‘Sonia’ of unknown flag, previously flying the flag of Tunisia, on its IUU vessel list.

This listing is the result of the consistent efforts for the reinforcement of the CoC and the establishment of the instruments to effectively fight IUU fishing in the Mediterranean, together with the increased presence of the EFCA’s patrol vessel.
